_doc: Nuclear forces per snapshot. stockpile = warheads available to the military (deployed + stored), excluding retired warheads awaiting dismantlement; this is what the engine uses. null = not published / not established.

USA.rationale: No no-first-use pledge; 2022 Nuclear Posture Review: use only in extreme circumstances to defend vital interests. Triad incl. SSBNs; B61 gravity bombs and air-launched cruise missiles.

RUS.rationale: 2020 Basic Principles and the November 2024 revision lowered the stated threshold (conventional attack threatening sovereignty, attacks by non-nuclear states backed by nuclear states). Large non-strategic arsenal (Iskander, Kinzhal), Avangard HGV, Oreshnik IRBM.

CHN.rationale: Unconditional no-first-use pledge in defence white papers. Road-mobile DF-41/DF-31, DF-26 IRBM, JL-3 SLBM.

GBR.rationale: Minimum deterrent, single Trident SLBM system, deliberate ambiguity on first use.

FRA.rationale: Strict sufficiency with a 'final warning' (ultime avertissement) pre-strategic strike capability via ASMP-A air-launched missiles; M51 SLBMs.

IND.rationale: 2003 doctrine: no first use (with a chemical/biological caveat), massive retaliation. Agni missiles; SSBN force still nascent, so not counted as an assured second strike.

PAK.rationale: 'Full spectrum deterrence', first use explicitly not ruled out, short-range Nasr for battlefield use.

ISR.rationale: Undeclared arsenal; widely assessed as last-resort. Jericho missiles; Dolphin-class submarines reportedly provide a sea-based leg.

PRK.rationale: September 2022 nuclear forces law permits pre-emptive use. Hwasong-17/18 ICBMs, tactical Hwasong-11 family.

2021._check: stockpiles sum to SIPRI's ~9,620 (North Korea taken at the midpoint of 40-50)

2026._check: stockpiles sum exactly to SIPRI's published 9,745

USA.note: Secondary coverage reports the total inventory inconsistently (5,042 / 5,177); stockpile and deployed figures agree across sources.

IND.note: First time SIPRI classified Indian warheads as deployed.
